content_ideas: Blog post announcing event with embedded video teaser

industry_best_practices.structure: Lead with the what/when/where hook in the first line, back it with one social-proof number (past attendance, speaker count) before secondary detail; subject lines name the event + a concrete driver ("Speak at KubeCon: CFP now open") rather than vague teasers.
industry_best_practices.cta_guidance: One primary CTA per email as a specific verb ("Submit a Proposal," "Reserve Your Spot") — not "Learn More"; secondary links (venue, travel grants) stay de-emphasized text links, not competing buttons.
industry_best_practices.urgency_fomo_tactics: No real deadline yet, so FOMO comes from momentum/scarcity-of-opportunity (CFP close date, "limited speaking slots," early-bird cutoff) plus social proof ("2,347 already registered") — never a manufactured countdown.
industry_best_practices.specificity_notes: Insist on named past speakers or a real quote, exact (not rounded) past-year attendance figures, and concrete submission guidelines (themes, formats) instead of "share your expertise" filler.

industry_best_practices.structure: Subject line carries the time pressure directly with a specific number ("5 hours left," "Registration closes tonight"); body opens with the deadline/price change, states the one action, reinforces with a second lighter urgency cue near the CTA.
industry_best_practices.cta_guidance: Exactly one CTA, imperative and time-bound ("Register Before Midnight," "Lock In Your Rate") — a single hard CTA is non-negotiable here.
industry_best_practices.urgency_fomo_tactics: Real tiered pricing that actually increases, genuine capacity caps ("only 40 seats left" — must stay true), escalating 4-email cadence (teaser → offer → countdown → last-chance), attendee/company social proof. Never state false scarcity.
industry_best_practices.specificity_notes: Use the actual price delta, actual seat/ticket counts, exact date/time with timezone, named confirmed speakers/sessions for that week.

industry_best_practices.structure: Thank-you within 24 hours, warm/authentic tone; survey ask follows 2-3 days later (own email or combined); recordings/content release is a separate wave 1-2 weeks out, built around a video thumbnail/highlight reel, not a plain link.
industry_best_practices.cta_guidance: One next-best action per email ("Take the Survey," "Watch the Replay") — CTA copy matches the content type; a visible video thumbnail near the CTA meaningfully lifts click rate.
industry_best_practices.urgency_fomo_tactics: No real deadline — replace urgency with reciprocity/incentive framing (survey-completion incentive) and segment attendees vs. no-shows ("you missed X, here's the recording" FOMO-lite for no-shows).
industry_best_practices.specificity_notes: Reference concrete session names, real attendee/session counts, a specific highlight moment or real quote/photo — avoid generic "what a great event" copy.

industry_best_practices.structure: Light, predictable cadence (monthly for long-horizon teasers); content reads as a community update (wins, upcoming CFP date, past-event callback), not a sales pitch.
industry_best_practices.cta_guidance: Subtle, low-friction CTA every time (join community channel, "note the date") rather than a hard conversion ask — presence of a soft CTA is fine, aggressiveness is not.
industry_best_practices.urgency_fomo_tactics: Aspirational, not clock-based — "CFP opens [month]," community-growth momentum framing, callbacks to what people got out of the last event.
industry_best_practices.specificity_notes: Anchor teaser copy to one real locked detail (confirmed date/city, theme, returning speaker) instead of "stay tuned" filler; use real community metrics (member count, meetups, contributor stats).
